```{r}
library(here)

# Scale high-resolution PNG files to the report column.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  out.width = "85%",
  fig.align = "center"
)

nearest_neighbors <- read.csv(
  here("results", "nearest_neighbors.csv")
)

gender_associations <- read.csv(
  here("results", "gender_associations.csv")
)

compression_metrics <- read.csv(
  here("results", "image_compression_metrics.csv")
)
```

## Project overview

This project explores two applications of singular value decomposition
(SVD):

1. Learning low-dimensional word embeddings from a word
   co-occurrence matrix.
2. Compressing a grayscale image using low-rank matrix
   approximations.

The text analysis uses the six novels included in the
`janeaustenr` package. Words that occur within a five-word window are
recorded in a weighted co-occurrence matrix. The 3,000 most frequent
non-stopwords are retained.

## Word embeddings

The co-occurrence matrix is transformed using

\[
\widetilde{M}_{ij} = \log(1 + M_{ij})
\]

and approximated using the top 100 singular components. The resulting
word vectors are normalized so cosine similarity can be used to compare
words.

### Singular values

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics(
  here("figures", "singular_values.png")
)
```

The rapid initial decline indicates that a relatively small number of
components captures a substantial portion of the matrix structure.
Later components contribute progressively smaller refinements.

### Nearest neighbours

```{r}
selected_neighbors <- subset(
  nearest_neighbors,
  target %in% c(
    "love",
    "marriage",
    "elizabeth",
    "darcy"
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  selected_neighbors,
  digits = 4,
  col.names = c(
    "Target",
    "Neighbour",
    "Cosine similarity"
  )
)
```

The model recovers several intuitive relationships. Words such as
`affection`, `attachment`, and `heart` appear near `love`, while major
characters from *Pride and Prejudice* form a recognizable cluster around
`elizabeth` and `darcy`.

## Gender associations

A gender direction is estimated by averaging several normalized
differences, including `woman - man`, `girl - boy`, and
`wife - husband`.

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics(
  here("figures", "gender_associations.png")
)
```

These projections describe patterns in this particular literary corpus.
They should not be interpreted as inherent characteristics of people or
concepts. The results can reflect historical language, character roles,
and the limited scope of the novels.

## Image compression

The built-in `volcano` topographic matrix is treated as a grayscale
image. Rank-\(k\) approximations are reconstructed using

\[
A_k = U_k \Sigma_k V_k^\top.
\]

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics(
  here("figures", "image_compression.png")
)
```

```{r}
compression_display <- compression_metrics

compression_display$relative_error <- paste0(
  round(
    100 * compression_display$relative_error,
    2
  ),
  "%"
)

compression_display$storage_saving <- paste0(
  round(
    100 * compression_display$storage_saving,
    2
  ),
  "%"
)

knitr::kable(
  compression_display,
  col.names = c(
    "Rank",
    "Relative error",
    "Stored values",
    "Storage saving"
  )
)
```

A rank-10 approximation reduces storage by approximately 72% while
keeping relative reconstruction error near 1.45%. At sufficiently high
ranks, the factorized representation becomes larger than the original
matrix.

## Limitations

The text results depend on the corpus, vocabulary size, context window,
stopword list, and embedding dimension. Jane Austen's novels represent a
specific historical and literary setting, so conclusions should not be
generalized to modern language or society.

The image example illustrates low-rank approximation on a small
topographic matrix. Performance on photographs and other complex images
may differ.

## Reproducibility

Run the scripts in numerical order:

```text
R/01_build_corpus.R
R/02_fit_embeddings.R
R/03_explore_embeddings.R
R/04_analyze_gender_associations.R
R/05_image_compression.R
```
